candidate_alignments.continuity: Both address the existence/non-existence of a niche; PRE is a denial, POST acknowledges a possible niche
candidate_alignments.scope: PRE scopes to absence; POST scopes to a specific population
candidate_alignments.frame: PRE = null/denial frame; POST = qualified-exception frame with a concrete audience
candidate_alignments.stretch: Stretching from a denial to a tentative exception with population specification

matched_pairs.basis: Both address niche status within target market; PRE denies a niche, POST provides a tentative exception in a specific audience. The audience scope shifts from 'none' to 'eco-friendly musicians.'

structural_development.rationale: PRE is a terse two-word denial ('No idea'). POST adds a qualified claim ('Not necessarily, other than maybe eco-friendly musicians'), introducing a specific audience segment and a hedge. This adds meaningful content (a specific niche and a qualifier) at the clause level, but the response remains a single short sentence. Moderate Addition rather than Significant, because only one new clause-level idea is added.

semantic_events.rationale: The PRE asserts no niche exists at all. The POST narrows the denial by carving out one possible exception: eco-friendly musicians. POST is a specific restricted version of PRE's broader claim (any niche possible → no niche, except this one). Scope restriction holds: POST's 'maybe eco-friendly musicians' is a proper subset of the broader 'any niche' space that PRE was denying. Subsumption test: 'an eco-friendly-musicians niche possibility is a specific way of being a niche possibility that PRE was broadly denying' — true. This is scope restriction, which outranks Reframed per the scoped_category rule. Alternative considered: Reframed (denial frame → qualified-exception frame), but scope restriction takes priority.

uncertainty.coder_notes: The PRE 'No idea' is genuinely terse and could be read as (a) 'I have no niche idea' or (b) a more general 'I don't know.' Read (a) supports the Narrowed reading because the POST then offers one niche idea as an exception to the broader denial. Read (b) would weaken the semantic event to possibly No Change or Reframed. Interpreted here as (a), which is the more domain-appropriate reading for a Q2.2 niche question. Flagged boundary_case_narrow_vs_reframe because the subsumption sentence is arguable.
